To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angular dependence of the photonic stop-band position in thin-film periodic structures leads to large coherence-area laser modes.
we demonstrate the possibility of large area coherent laser emission from thin film structures with large coherence areas.

the shift of a stop-band with increasing angle results in a wide exponential field distribution corresponding only to strong angular confinement, that the beam expansion follows a diffusive equation, and that the size of the beam is limited only by that of the gain area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel photonic structures and devices.
the development of new photonic devices based on thin films.
the design of novel optical devices based on the interaction of light with photonic bandgap materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the angular confinement of the light field in a thin periodic medium with a large coherence area is determined by the spectral width of the stop-band and is independent of the size of the medium.
the angular confinement of radiation in photonic structures is a general property of the stop-band effect and that it is not restricted to a specific class of photonic structures.
the large coherence area of the periodic structure is the key to the large transverse field distribution and to the large beam divergence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that a large coherence area can be achieved by the combination of two effects: (1) the large coherence length in a photonic stop-band and (2) the angular confinement of the emission in a periodic structure.
we have demonstrated the first photonic stopband laser.
we have demonstrated the first thin film photonic stop-band laser with a large coherence area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thin film lasers can be designed to have large coherence areas, and hence, large beam areas.
the angular selectivity of the stop-band is the key to achieving large coherence area in thin films.
the angular confinement in photonic stop-band structures can be exploited to achieve large coherence-area lasers with a wide range of applications.
